text: The highest-priority AI Layer 1 universe should avoid a GPU-only framing and instead emphasize packaging/test, HBM yield control, photonics/CPO manufacturing, and reference demand anchors.
Advanced packaging, OSAT, probe cards, processor test, HBM inspection, and metrology are currently the strongest evidenced underfollowed AI chokepoint lane in the provided Layer 1B material.
Compound photonics and CPO remain a valid underfollowed discovery lane, but several company mappings require primary-source verification because evidence is mostly from secondary search context.

Layer 1 universe remains narrow because power, cooling, grid interconnection, data-center construction, and vertical AI automation software candidates were not visible in the provided Layer 1B excerpt.
Layer 2 should add current market-cap, liquidity, analyst-coverage, valuation, backlog, customer qualification, utilization, pricing, and capex checks before ranking investability.

For AI, use hyperscalers, GPU vendors, custom ASIC vendors, and foundries as demand anchors, but map bottleneck research below them into packaging, substrates, HBM test, photonics, power, and qualification gates.
Highest-priority Layer 2A bottleneck candidates: advanced packaging capacity, ABF substrates/materials, HBM-related test/probe/inspection, photonics/InP capacity, and data-center power transformers.

Low-attention supplier lanes to preserve for later layers: inspection/metrology, probe cards, thermal test handlers, OSAT overflow, advanced packaging bonding tools, MOCVD epitaxy, III-V etch/deposition, and qualified transformer suppliers.

Most important catalyst class is hard customer evidence: long-term supply agreements, capacity reservations, customer advance payments, qualification wins, AI/HPC backlog, or explicit HBM/advanced-packaging/optical-interconnect revenue commentary.

Need primary-source verification from company filings and earnings calls for each underfollowed candidate before any company survives Layer 2B: revenue mix, customer concentration, backlog, capacity, lead times, qualification status, and gross-margin impact.
Power-equipment AI exposure needs careful separation between generic electrification/grid demand and AI-specific data-center demand; qualified supplier lists and backlog attribution are required.
CPO and III-V-on-silicon names should remain hypotheses unless supported by customer contracts, production qualification, shipment volumes, or credible capacity reservation evidence.

CAMT should remain a high-priority underfollowed AI chokepoint candidate mapped to HBM, chiplet, hybrid-bonding, and advanced-packaging inspection/metrology; next gate is primary-source verification of AI-specific order durability and backlog quality.

COHU should remain a high-priority underfollowed AI test candidate mapped to thermal test, high-socket-force handling, inspection/metrology, interface solutions, and HBM inspection; next gate is evidence of repeat AI/HPC platform adoption across multiple customers.

FORM should remain an underfollowed AI test-hardware candidate mapped to HBM probe cards, logic/foundry probe cards, advanced package test, and possible silicon-photonics test; next gate is evidence that HBM probe demand is supply constrained and structurally durable.

AMKR should be treated as a reference advanced-packaging and OSAT capacity candidate rather than a clean underfollowed small/mid-cap; next gate is durable AI/HPC revenue conversion from high-density fan-out, advanced test, and Arizona capacity.

6239.TW should remain a hypothesis-stage underfollowed OSAT candidate tied to memory backend crowding-out, fan-out panel-level packaging, AI/HPC packaging overflow, and possible CPO exposure; primary-source validation is required.
KLIC should remain a hypothesis-stage advanced-packaging equipment candidate; verify whether HBM-related tools and advanced solutions are material enough to offset legacy wire-bond cyclicality.
AIXA.DE should remain a hypothesis-stage upstream AI photonics equipment candidate mapped to MOCVD/epitaxy for III-V photonics and CPO; verify AI optical-interconnect-specific backlog and lead times.

ALMU should remain a speculative shadow candidate only; evidence must confirm commercial readiness, customer contracts, production qualification, revenue scale, and balance-sheet runway before it can graduate.

OXIG.L should remain a hypothesis-stage photonics process-tool candidate mapped to III-V etch/deposition and CPO manufacturing; verify order intake and backlog specifically tied to datacenter optical interconnect.
The supplied candidate chunk is truncated after Coherent; Coherent and any following candidates should not be fully mapped without the complete Layer 1 candidate records or primary-source evidence.

Need current market capitalization, liquidity, valuation, short interest, analyst coverage, and institutional ownership checks for all names before confirming underfollowed status or market-pricing asymmetry.

Need primary-source filings/transcripts for Powertech, Aixtron, Aeluma, Oxford Instruments, Kulicke & Soffa, and Coherent because the current evidence mostly supports node-level bottlenecks or cached Layer 1 hypotheses rather than company-level AI revenue attribution.

Layer 2C should test falsification signals across the chunk: easing lead times, inventory build, customer insourcing, lower AI/HPC order mix, margin compression, delayed customer qualification, cancelled capex, or evidence that demand is cyclical rather than structurally bottlenecked.

AVGO should remain in the AI theme graph as a reference demand anchor, not an underfollowed Serenity target; its custom AI accelerator and AI networking disclosures are useful for validating upstream bottlenecks in foundry, advanced packaging, substrates, test, HBM backend, and network connectivity.

HUBN.SW should remain in the underfollowed lane as a hypothesis mapped to optical connectivity, data-center connectivity, and possible CPO-adjacent infrastructure, but its AI revenue exposure and customer qualifications need primary-source verification before promotion.

Need current Huber+Suhner primary-source evidence: annual report, segment revenue, backlog, management commentary, hyperscaler/switch OEM qualifications, product references to 800G/1.6T, CPO, silicon photonics, AI data centers, or optical interconnect applications.

Need Broadcom primary filing confirmation from FY2026 Q2 10-Q and earnings transcript for exact custom AI accelerator revenue language, remaining performance obligations, purchase commitments, customer concentration, and supply-chain capacity constraints.

For both tickers, Layer 2C should add market-pricing checks: current market cap, valuation, analyst coverage, revenue purity, short interest, liquidity, and whether the AI exposure is already fully recognized by the market.
